affectedSurfaces: builder critic Runtime Probe artifact emission
Runtime Probe run-directory containment and stageability validation
hypothesis: Re-resolving the real artifact parent after probe execution and performing every mutation relative to an isolated process cwd verified against the captured run-directory inode will preserve committed Runtime Probe evidence while preventing builder-controlled links, special files, or raced parent components from redirecting the daemon's artifact write.

metricsCompared.name: artifact redirection regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: The pre-execution lexical stageability check accepted runtime-probe.json links, and writeFileSync followed either a pre-planted or probe-created link into an external daemon-user-writable target.
metricsCompared.candidate: Focused cases execute the probe, reject pre-planted and probe-created artifact links, preserve the external target byte-for-byte, reject a probe-created non-regular artifact, reject a probe-created run-directory link that resolves outside the real workspace, and simulate a parent-path swap after capturing the legitimate run-directory inode.

metricsCompared.name: artifact write boundary
metricsCompared.baseline: Artifact containment was lexical, checked only before execution, and the final pathname write followed links without checking the opened inode.
metricsCompared.candidate: The final path is rebuilt from real workspace and run-directory paths after execution; builder stageability is checked again; an isolated helper verifies its cwd against the captured run-directory inode; and all writes and atomic installation use relative names within that stable kernel directory reference.
metricsCompared.unit: filesystem invariants asserted by production code and focused tests

rationale: This is a fail-closed correction to an existing Safety boundary, not a new probe capability. The pre-execution ignored-path gate remains to avoid running a probe whose evidence cannot be committed, while every result path now repeats real-path containment and stageability checks after execution. Final writes run in an isolated process whose cwd must match the captured run-directory inode; all filesystem mutations use relative names, and a private no-follow temporary regular file is atomically renamed into place only after the existing entry and absolute run-directory path are revalidated. The focused suite demonstrates both attacker-controlled symlink timings, a parent-directory escape, and the exact capture-then-parent-swap race without modifying the external target; the broader Runtime Probe suite preserves trusted, rejected, failed, ignored, sandbox, coredump, hard-link, runner, parser, and toolchain behavior.
